questions.question: Explain why a person who touches a bare illegal cable is more likely to die than a person who touches a faulty appliance in a properly wired house.
questions.expected_answer: In a properly wired house the earth wire carries fault current to earth and the earth leakage unit switches the supply off within a fraction of a second when about 30 mA leaks. An illegal cable has no earth wire, no breaker and no earth leakage unit, so the current through the person (far more than the roughly 50 mA that can stop the heart) keeps flowing.

questions.question: Give two ways in which illegal connections harm people who pay for their electricity.
questions.expected_answer: They overload transformers, which burn out or explode and leave the whole area without power, and they lead to load reduction; the cost of stolen electricity is recovered through higher tariffs and less money for municipal services.

questions.question: A cable is lying across a path to school. State what learners should do and why.
questions.expected_answer: Treat it as live: do not touch, step on or move it, keep others (especially younger children) away, and report it to Eskom or the municipality. It may carry 230 V or more with no protection, so touching it could be fatal.
